speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, please describe the painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg in detail. When did it first appear, and has it changed in size, color, or drainage since then?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes, and recent corticosteroid use, I am concerned about an atypical infection. When you mention an "ant bite," was there actually an insect stinger visible, or did a small scratch or bite precede the lesion?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis (Old World)

The description of a painful, ulcerative lesion with a central necrotic base, purplish irregular borders, and a history of an insect bite in a patient with diabetes is highly suggestive of leishmaniasis. I need to confirm the specific appearance of the ulcer's edges and check for systemic symptoms like fever or night sweats to rule out other atypical infections or malignancy.
